Create the file case_120.inp in the working directory using exactly the input deck content provided, preserving all whitespace, node coordinates, element connectivity, boundary conditions, material properties, and the empty *STEP / *END STEP block verbatim.
Do not modify any physics, topology, material values, or step definitions in the input deck.
Run CalculiX by executing the command ccx -i case_120 in the working directory; if that invocation is not recognized, fall back to ccx case_120.
After the run completes (or fails), read the file case_120.sta and search for the string JOB COMPLETED to determine success; if the string is absent, treat the run as a failure.
Capture the CalculiX version string by running ccx -v (or the closest equivalent such as ccx --version) and store it for the results file.
Write a file named results.json in the working directory containing a JSON object with the following keys: solver set to the string calculix, case_id set to the string case_120, status set to the string success if JOB COMPLETED was found in the .sta file or the string error otherwise, ccx_version set to the version string captured from ccx -v, artifacts set to an empty array, and notes set to a string that records the exact ccx command used; if the run failed, append the error message from the .sta or .msg file and name the file that indicated the failure.
Do not alter the input deck to add loads, procedure keywords, or any other content; run the deck exactly as provided.
